query: Starting from an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state and a target density below 6 g/cm3, what single intervention could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts measurable changes relative to the as-processed baseline, defines the relevant composition, temperature, exposure-time, and test-environment boundaries, cites supporting evidence from previously reported Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys, and proposes a controlled experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The single intervention that could overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation while improving room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys is the addition of a small amount of a refractory element, such as Nb or Ti, to the alloy system.
generation.material_initial_state: As-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state
generation.intervention: Addition of a small amount of a refractory element, such as Nb or Ti
generation.conditions: Room temperature, high-temperature oxidation environment, and corrosive environment
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a stable solid-solution phase and a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: Derived from materials-science principles, the addition of a refractory element can improve the stability of the solid-solution phase and enhance the formation of a protective oxide layer, leading to improved corrosion resistance and high-temperature oxidation resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
generation.boundary: Alloy composition, processing state, and test conditions
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of refractory element to be added and the optimal processing conditions are uncertain and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of refractory elements, such as Nb or Ti, and test their room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of a refractory element does not improve the room-temperature compressive behavior, corrosion resistance, and resistance to high-temperature oxidation, then the hypothesis is falsified
